title: Configurable PII scrubbers and audit-event sampling for embeddings + rerank pipeline
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Summary: Add server-side, configurable PII scrubbing modes and audit-event sampling controls to the embeddings and reranking endpoints. Goal is to give customers deterministic knobs to reduce risk (minimize sensitive token logging), meet retention policies, and retain fidelity for post-hoc investigations while keeping token-latency and throughput within SLA targets. This ticket scopes the API/console controls, runtime redaction pipeline, audit-event sampler, and a migration plan for existing telemetry streams.

Problem: Current telemetry and debug events for embeddings/rerank include raw request text or long spans that may contain PII. Some customers require stricter controls (no raw text persisted, short TTLs, hashed fingerprints only) while others want richer events for troubleshooting. There's no per-customer configuration to control what is logged, how long it's retained, or how frequently full-audit events are sampled. This leads to either too lax defaults or burdensome manual opt-outs.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals: Provide three scrub modes (none, token-hash, regex-redact) and a light/detailed audit-sampling policy configurable per-tenant; support configurable retention TTLs for raw payloads, embeddings, and hashed artifacts; expose these knobs in Console and API; ensure redaction happens as close to ingress as possible to avoid sensitive data spills; add metrics and dashboards to prove latency/regression impact.
- Non-goals: This ticket does NOT implement differential-privacy mechanisms for embedding vectors (future work) nor change model behavior. It also does not change external billing or public API surface beyond new query params/configs for enterprise tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant configuration exists that supports three scrub modes: none, token-hash, regex-redact
Audit-event sampler can be configured with an integer percentage and deterministic seed per tenant
Retention TTL settings available for raw request payloads, derived embeddings, and audit artifacts
Redaction pipeline runs before any long-term log persistence or external telemetry export
Latency impact must be <= 6ms median per request on p50 for our 512-token baseline in canary region
Automated e2e tests plus a privacy regression test that injects synthetic PII to validate scrubbers
Console UI and API docs updated with examples and migration guide
Security review completed and signed-off by Security team
Dashboard (Console) shows scrub-mode distribution, sampled audit rate, and retention metrics
implementation_notes: Add a lightweight redaction middleware in front of embedding/rerank handlers that can apply one of: regex-based redact (configurable regex list), token-level stable hash (HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-specific key), or pass-through
Ensure HMAC keys are tenant-scoped and stored in KMS; key rotation strategy documented
Audit sampler implemented as probabilistic deterministic sampler (hash(request_id) % 100 < sample_pct) to allow reproducible sampling decisions for debugging
Store three tiers of artifacts with separate retention: ephemeral (7 days), medium (30/90 days configurable), long (365 days) — by default do not store raw text beyond ephemeral unless tenant opts in
Telemetry exporters must honor scrub-mode; add unit tests asserting no plaintext in exports when regex-redact or token-hash mode enabled
Add async pipeline for expensive redaction rules to avoid blocking hot path; default to sync token-hash for latency-critical requests
Update routing and fallback to ensure that when migration toggles are flipped, legacy logs are backfilled carefully (see rollout plan)
qa_test_plan: Unit tests for each scrub-mode (regex, token-hash, none) with sample PII phrases
Integration tests that assert no raw text persists to S3/Cold storage for tenants with 'regex-redact' or 'token-hash' mode
Load test at 2x expected peak to validate async redaction queue doesn't cause backpressure
Canary rollout to 5% of tenants with telemetry comparing latencies and error rates vs control
Privacy regression test: inject synthetic SSNs/emails and verify removal/hashing in all logs and exports
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Implement middleware + sampler behind feature flag; unit & integration tests. Phase 2: Console controls + API surface; controlled canary with non-critical tenants; monitor latency and export correctness. Phase 3: Broader rollout to enterprise tenants with migration runbook to backfill or purge existing artifacts. Phase 4: Mandatory default tightening (e.g., default to token-hash for new tenants) after 6 weeks of telemetry. Emergency rollback: disable sampler and feature flag; purge newly created artifacts. Backfill strategy documented in Confluence link.
